subject: Request: Extended debug-log retention for forensic window (Medalys)
messages:
Date: Mon, 24 Nov 2025 09:15:00 -0800
From: Amelia Chen <legal@medalys.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Subject: Request: Extended debug-log retention for forensic window (Medalys)

Hi Priya,

We're preparing for an upcoming regulatory review and need to confirm whether Medalys can obtain an extended forensic window for debug/audit logs tied to our tenant. Our compliance team is asking for the ability to retain certain debug and request-level traces for 180 days (default noted in your docs is 30 days).

Specifically, could you confirm: 
- Which classes of logs can be retained beyond the 30-day default (request traces, KV cache evictions, model inference traces, error-level traces)?
- Whether Redwood can provide a signed proof-of-delete if records are later purged?
- What evidence/artifacts you can supply to satisfy SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ requests around retention and deletion (control mappings, runbooks, proof-of-delete manifests, storage location and chain-of-custody)?

We'd prefer the retention to remain in-region (US) and would be open to either Redwood-hosted extended retention or automated daily snapshot exports to our S3 bucket if that's an easier path. Please advise feasibility, a high-level approach, and any cost/contract implications.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

—Amelia
Amelia Chen
Legal & Compliance
Medalys Health
Date: Tue, 25 Nov 2025 10:02:00 -0800
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Chen <legal@medalys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Request: Extended debug-log retention for forensic window (Medalys)

Hi Amelia — thanks for the note and context. Looping in Ben and Marissa to confirm implementation and evidence artifacts. High-level answers below so you have something to review before we flesh out an evidence pack: 

1) Classes of logs: By default our hosted API retains ephemeral debug traces (default 30d). We can categorize logs into: request-level traces, debug traces (stack/param dumps), system operational metrics, and persistent audit events. Request-level traces and debug traces are the ones you referenced and are the most sensitive.

2) Retention options we can offer: 
  a) Hosted extended retention: For hosted customers we can make an exception and set tenant-scoped retention to 180 days for the relevant log classes. This introduces storage and cost implications and requires a formal exception/PO.
  b) Snapshot export: For hosted customers who prefer not to store extended logs on Redwood, we can deliver daily encrypted snapshots and push to your customer-controlled S3 (US region). You would retain them for the 180-day window.
  c) Dedicated/Private: If Medalys is on Dedicated or Private, tenant-retained logs can be configured for longer windows with more controls (KMS, HSM).

3) Proof-of-delete: We can produce a proof-of-delete manifest (SHA256 hashes of exported files, signed by Redwood's signing key, timestamped) and an operational runbook describing deletion procedures. For exports you control, we can provide a deletion attestation when you confirm purge from your S3.

4) Evidence we can supply: SOC 2 control mappings for retention, CAIQ snippets showing data location and processing, SIG artifacts (evidence snapshots), runbooks for retention/deletion, and manifest examples. We'll gather these in a single bundle once we align on the route.

Next steps from our side: Ben will confirm feasibility and ops impact. Marissa will assemble the evidence list and a preliminary retention matrix. Can you confirm which log classes you need retained, whether the export-to-S3 option would be acceptable, and whether you require Redwood to host the extended window? Also confirm the compliance cutoff date for the review.

If it's helpful we can scope costs for both the hosted-extension and snapshot-export approaches so you can decide.

Best,

—Priya Natarajan
Senior Trust & Safety Program Manager
Redwood Inference
Date: Wed, 26 Nov 2025 14:18:00 -0800
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Request: Extended debug-log retention for forensic window (Medalys)

Priya / team — quick technical note on feasibility and implementation paths. 

Summary: Both options Amelia described are doable; trade-offs below.

Option A — Redwood-hosted extended retention (tenant-scoped):
- We can configure tenant-level retention per-log-class up to 365 days; however, hosted tenants with longer retention increase storage cost and slightly higher RTO for large-scale replays.
- Requires an internal change ticket (config + monitoring) and an acceptance of a monthly storage uplift.
- We'll apply in-region residency (US) and use customer-specific KMS wrapping if requested (customer-managed keys require Private/Dedicated).
- We can provide proof-of-delete by capturing file-level manifests and producing a signed digest when deletion runs complete.

Option B — Daily encrypted snapshot exports to customer S3:
- We can ship daily snapshots (AES-256 encrypted, signed metadata) to your S3. Snapshots are incremental and include request-level traces for the specified classes.
- This approach minimizes Redwood-hosted storage and is quicker to provision for hosted customers.
- We will provide a playbook describing snapshot format, retention labeling, and a sample manifest you can verify.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Hosted live retention for 180 days: ~3–6 business days to provision; needs PO/exception and an updated data processing addendum for audit trails.
- Snapshot export: ~2 business days to enable exports + S3 bucket IAM config from Medalys. We will provide a short-run test with a 7‑day window first.

Artifacts we can produce immediately for your SIG/SOC2 pack: 
- retention_implementation_notes.md (technical design)
- snapshot_playbook.pdf (snapshot format and validation steps)
- example proof-of-delete manifest (template)

I'll attach the implementation notes and playbook to the evidence bundle Marissa will assemble. If Medalys elects the export route, we will need Jared's S3 bucket ARN and an IAM role to push snapshots.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: retention_implementation_notes.md, snapshot_playbook.pdf)

What we need from Medalys to proceed quickly:

- Which exact classes to include (proposed default: request-level traces + error-level debug only; exclude raw model context unless explicitly requested).

Timeline estimates once we have your decision and required artifacts:
